Binomial Option Tree

Black–ScholesProbabilityAlgorithms
Game: Price an option by chopping a year into steps where the stock can only go up or down, then working backwards from the end. How many steps until the answer stops changing?
How to play: Choose the number of steps and the option, and watch the tree and the graph below it.

Stock price above each node, the option's value below it.

The tree's price for 1 to 100 steps; dashed: Black–Scholes.

Look for the math

One step of up-or-down is too crude for a real stock, so use many short ones. This is the binomial model of Cox, Ross and Rubinstein (1979). The stock here starts at $100, and the option ends in one year.

Steps that match the volatility

Split the year into n steps of length dt. In each step the stock goes up by a factor u = eσ√dt or down by d = 1/u. That makes the spread of its log grow like σ² per year, just as in the Stock Price Paths page. After n steps the end prices are S uj dn−j: a binomial spread of outcomes.

Working backwards

At the end the option is worth its payoff. One step earlier, the riskless hedge of the previous page prices each node from the two after it: the discounted average with the risk-neutral chance q = (er dt − d)/(u − d). Repeat back to today. At every node the hedge is Δ = (Vup − Vdown)/(Sup − Sdown) shares, so the hedge must be adjusted at every step. An American put can also be exercised early, so each node takes the larger of holding on and exercising now.

The limit is Black–Scholes

As the steps get shorter, the binomial spread becomes a normal one (the de Moivre–Laplace theorem), and the tree's price tends to

C = S N(d1) − K e−rT N(d2)

The graph shows the tree's price zigzagging above and below the formula as the steps alternate odd and even. The logic test checked a 10,000-step tree to within 0.001 of $10.4506. It also checked that every node's hedge copies the option exactly one step later, and that calls and puts satisfy C − P = S − K e−rT.

Choose a put with 10% interest and tick American. Where in the tree is it worth exercising early?
